evidence.quote:
To be successful , it is very important for you to follow the following rules :
1. First , reason out how you want to condense the Observation for the current state
    and what information you need to add , if any .
2. Next , present one Condensed Observation in the following form : info [< Condensed
    Observation >]
3. Do not remove navigating buttons since the agent must be able to go back and
    forth between pages .
4. When there is a long list of options or products in the webpage , try to retain
    only a couple of them in the Condensed Observation based on the Instruction and
    Previous Action of Agent .
5. If " Invalid Action " is found in the Observation , add hint within info [< Condensed
    Observation >] to help the agent perform the correct action .
6. Always add ( to click ) after the attribute name like color , size , etc . in the
    Condensed Observation .
evidence.support_explanation: Complete operational rules keep navigation buttons, use previous action, add invalid-action hints and emit info[]. These are quoted prompt data, never executed.

signatures.object: Current WebShop text-rich observation passed to actor
signatures.information: Summarizer sees instruction, previous action and current raw page; stateless, no future states or gold success labels. Actor sees goal and accumulated summarized observations/actions, not full raw pages.
signatures.operation: Frozen LM prompted with page-type examples extracts matching attributes, keeps about three relevant search products, prunes incompatible options, retains navigation controls and adds invalid-action hints.
signatures.conditions: Raw page must fit summarizer context; relevant options must survive selection and be represented truthfully.
signatures.feedback: Current environment text, including Invalid Action; not an external success judge.
signatures.selection_rule: LM relevance judgments conditioned on instruction and previous action; approximately three products; no calibrated threshold or acceptance audit.
signatures.selection_data: Fixed hand-authored prompt examples in Appendix C; 50 of stated 500 trajectories used in model pilot per Appendix A.
signatures.persistence: Per-episode summarized history in actor prompt only; frozen reusable templates. No cross-task learned memory, weight update or retained self-improvement.
signatures.later_use: Later steps in same episode read summarized history.
signatures.claimed_effect: Higher task success and average score, fewer repeated invalid actions, especially lengthy histories.
signatures.failure_boundary: Summarizer can repeat long lists or hallucinate nonexistent target options; no grounding filter or raw-observation fallback is described.

signatures.information: Goal plus alternating summarized observations and actions; same frozen backbone as comparator within each model condition.
signatures.operation: Greedy actor emits search, click or think; execute environment transition, summarize new text, append to history; stop on purchase / cap / repeated invalid actions.
signatures.output: Executed WebShop trajectory and terminal product-attribute reward
signatures.conditions: 20-step cap, five consecutive invalid actions terminate; max generated tokens 500; usable structured button names.
signatures.feedback: Actual simulator observation each step; terminal benchmark score compares bought product to requested attributes.
signatures.selection_rule: Greedy decoding, not best-of-N or verifier reranking.
signatures.selection_data: Prompt demonstrations, no policy training reported.
signatures.persistence: Episode-local history; no accepted/rejected policy candidates or persistent updates.
signatures.later_use: Subsequent decisions within same episode only; retained-gain chain not_applicable to static prompting contribution.
signatures.claimed_effect: CODE-DAVINCI-002 SR 23.4 to 30.2; GPT-3.5-TURBO SR 3.0 to 12.6 in Table 1.
signatures.failure_boundary: Purchases are irreversible episode endings; full real websites / unseen site transfer not tested; cost and repeated-run evidence absent.

gap.author_gap: Earlier prompted decision agents focus on action representation / thought generation while passing lengthy noisy raw observations to a single actor; these overload context and distract action choice.
gap.checked_gap: Paper supplies concrete WebShop invalid-action and context-limit observations plus an executable comparator on two backbones. It does not independently establish that previous methods universally preserve full observations; nearest source originals are missing from the fixed input set.

lineage.relation: Closest comparator; think-act prompting. Authors reimplement with CODE-DAVINCI-002 rather than original PaLM; no original fulltext provided.
lineage.source_strength: author_report in P1 §6 and Appendix A, not independently checked

lineage.relation: Inherited e-commerce environment, action interface and terminal attribute score; fulltext not in supplied 14-reference inventory.
lineage.source_strength: author_report in P1 §4 and Appendix F

lineage.source: Multi-stage prompting for knowledgeable dialogue generation, 2203.08745; MSP translation prompting, 2110.06609
lineage.relation: Authors acknowledge staged prompting precedents outside navigation; original source claims not independently verified.

gap.closest_adjacent: ReAct is the direct contemporary comparator. Shared references.json contains Mind2Web 2306.06070 and WebArena 2307.13854, but neither is evidence of the missing ReAct/WebShop original method and neither is used as ASH's own contribution.
gap.residue: Whether explicit action-aware semantic condensation helps beyond another LM call, added prompt hints or simple matched-budget truncation/top-k filtering, and whether it remains faithful on complex pages.
gap.stakes: Token-window exhaustion, hallucinated unavailable actions and premature purchase of partly matching products prevent task completion.
gap.method_response: Separate stateless page condensation from stateful action generation, keeping only goal-relevant page content in all subsequent actor history.
gap.remaining_gap: No direct faithfulness/target-recall audit; no equal-call / token-budget alternative; no unseen-site validation; long-trajectory bins use achieved rather than independent reference length.
unresolved: Controller must supply version-fixed ReAct 2210.03629 and WebShop 2207.01206 original fulltexts to BOTH seats to complete independent nearest-neighbor/gap verification. No unilateral external retrieval performed.

claims.text: ASH outperforms prior prompting on WebShop.
claims.setting: Text-rich full-product WebShop; CODE-DAVINCI-002 and GPT-3.5-TURBO-0613; greedy; max 500 generation tokens; 20 actions / five invalid termination.
claims.baseline/control: Authors' own ReAct reproduction using same backbone; original PaLM implementation not run.
claims.selection_vs_test: Fixed stated 500 trajectories; 50 of them used in model choice pilot, not disjoint development. Prompt selection split not specified.
counterevidence: Abstract states 6.2%, Table 1 and body support 6.8 percentage points for CODE-DAVINCI-002.
Appendix F loop describes 499 iterations; exact denominator unresolved.
No repeated-run uncertainty; extra summarizer call not compute matched.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Author-reported executable WebShop comparison favors ASH in these two fixed-LM conditions; not a reproduction or general live-web improvement.

claims.selection_vs_test: Failure categories computed on same evaluated trajectories.
counterevidence: Percentages are described as shares of failures, not all task attempts; failure denominators differ.
The summarizer itself hallucinates nonexistent sizes; no overall faithfulness audit or mechanistic noise control.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Reported share of failures attributed to repeated invalid actions decreases; no general hallucination-elimination conclusion.

claims.text: ASH helps lengthy histories and mitigates need for explicit actor reasoning.
claims.setting: Figure 4 achieved-trajectory length bins and Figure 5b Direct ablation
claims.baseline/control: Direct SR22.2, ReAct23.4, Direct+ASH27.4; full ASH30.2 in Table 1
claims.selection_vs_test: Same evaluation; trajectory length is endogenous to agent decisions, not held-out reference difficulty.
counterevidence: Conditioning on achieved length can select different tasks/failures per agent.
Summarizer still explicitly reasons; Direct actor is not a reasoning-free system.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Useful within-suite ablation and association support a simplified actor with a summarizer; not causal proof of better intrinsic long-horizon ability or removal of system-level reasoning.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Authors report a fixed, executable text-rich WebShop evaluation where action-aware current-page summarization improves their ReAct/Direct prompting baselines on two frozen models. Full prompts and failures are provided. This supports an online simulator result, not Mind2Web dataset evidence, unseen-site transfer, general hallucination reduction, or retained improvement.
unresolved: Independent nearest-neighbor/source verification pending shared ReAct/WebShop fulltexts.
PDF equation / chart-only data unknown; abstract-main gain discrepancy and exact sample count unresolved.
No contamination audit, disjoint selection holdout, repeated-run uncertainty, pruning recall or measured inference cost.
Protocol draft status prevents treating these working ratings as frozen calibrated final scores.

Full templates and honest summarizer failures improve reconstructibility. Causal attribution, independent selection holdout, statistical reliability and extra-call cost accounting remain limited; transfer and retained gains are unsupported.
